description.narrative: Sanitation program that aims at achieving scalability of decentralized sustainable sanitation at the national level and establish financial mechanisms that allow families to access a decentralized sanitation solution.

Sanitetsprogram som syftar till att uppnå skalbarhet för decentraliserad hållbar sanitet på nationell nivå och etablera finansiella mekanismer som gör det möjligt för familjer att få tillgång till en decentraliserad sanitetslösning.

The General Objective of the second phase is to achieve:
Scalability of the Decentralized Sustainable Sanitation at the national level and establish financial mechanisms that allow families to access a decentralized sanitation solution.
Specific objectives:
- Consolidation* of the decentralized sustainable urban sanitation scalability model and its most relevant components: governance, adoption and behaviour change, climate resilience, and circular economy.
- Replicability of the decentralized sustainable urban and rural sanitation model in at least three new municipalities.
- Maximize the leverage of economic resources destined to scale the decentralized sustainable sanitation
- Involvement of the financial sector in the implementation of an innovative financial mechanisms for the implementation of the decentralized sustainable sanitation model.
*Consolidation shall mean (a) the formal adoption of the model by municipal authorities and service providers; (b) allocation of own budgets by GAMs and families; (c) appropriate use of services, including improvement of Hygiene practices/Menstrual Hygiene Management practices; and d) Payment of fees

sector.narrative: Water supply and sanitation - large systems

description.narrative:
During this initial implementation period, significant progress has been made, reflecting the commitment of local authorities, technical and social stakeholders, as well as the institutional and financial support of UNICEF and its strategic partners.
The Ministry of Environment and Water (MMAyA) has issued Ministerial Resolution 551/2024 which validates the decentralized sanitation model along with its technical guidelines and protocols. Additionally, the Menstrual Hygiene Management Guide has been approved through RM 550/2024, strengthening the legal framework for nationwide implementation.
The municipalities of Montero and Cobija have served as key settings for the demonstration and consolidation of the model. In both cases, effective multisectoral governance and municipal budgetary commitment have proven to be critical factors for sustainability.
Montero has secured co-financing through its Water and Sanitation Directorate. Cobija has promoted innovative practices, such as the production of organic fertilizer from dry fecal waste.
UNICEF has made progress in building partnerships and initiating resource mobilization efforts with multilateral and bilateral partners, reinforcing the programs financial foundation.
Ongoing training has been provided to municipal and community personnel, alongside efforts to strengthen the technical and social capacities of EPSAs. These actions aim to ensure operational quality and mitigate the impact of high staff turnover.
The program maintains a strategic communication line focused on CBS, addressing sociocultural barriers and promoting the acceptance and proper use of sustainable sanitation technologies. This strategy also includes the promotion of hygiene practices, with particular emphasis on menstrual health.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
